Q: Find index of last element in vector below threshold A:

We might want to use Position(), one of those Common Higher-Order Functions in Functional Programming Languages which we tend to forget.

Position(\(x) x<8L, v, right=TRUE)

[1] 7

Comes with a nomatch argument, default set to NA.

Q: Does Datacap have a way to read searchable pdf instead of using OCR? A:

Extraction of text within a searchable PDF without performing OCR can be done by setting the @X.y_contentReuseMode to the value 2, prior to calling an OCRA action to perform recognition.

For reference : RecognitionOCRA - Options available for y_ContentReuseMode

Example with Recognize() to create a file with the PDF text & read it into a Datacap variable:

rrSet("2", "@X.y_contentReuseMode")
Recognize() // Creates a layout file containing PDF text
CreateCCOFromLayout() // Convert layout to CCO
NormalizeCCO() // Rearange text in natural reading order
// Note: If some text gets dropped (check RSS logs) -> you might need to use `SetMaxCharacterHeightTMM()` action or its other "AVG" variant.
CreateTextFile() // Create a pure text file with the PDF text content.
ReadTextFile("@PILOT(BATCHDIR)+\+@P.ID+.txt", "@X.your_var") // Read text file content into a variable

Note: this should also works with PDFFREDocumentToImage() action, that will directly output a CCO file by default for each page. Or can instruct it to generate the an intermediate layout file by using rrSet("1", "@X.y_createLayout").

Q: SwiftUI MVVM: Should form input fields be stored in @State or @Published properties in the ViewModel? A:

Actually neither of these approaches.

Normally the Task would be a model object and you would bind its properties like it's title to Views like TextField.

You could actually just rename CreateTaskViewModel to TaskModel (don't use Task because that will conflict with async/await's Task.

Q: Is idempotency really necessary for preventing duplicate payments in a typical shopping mall application? A:

I understand the general principle that client-side actions should not be trusted.

However, doesn't the same argument apply to client-generated idempotency keys?

If a malicious client can bypass the disabled button and directly craft requests, it could also generate a new idempotency key for every request.

From a security perspective, I'm struggling to see how client-generated idempotency keys provide stronger protection than client-side duplicate-submit prevention.

Is the assumption that the server pre-registers or associates idempotency keys with a specific payment attempt?
